item.title: Work to commence on Roscommon route later this year
item.description: Plans to upgrade a key stretch in Roscommon town are expected to advance this year. The proposed works focus on the route linking the area near Hannon’s Hotel to the Golf Links Road, a section that has long been highlighted by residents and road users as requiring improvement. The project will proceed to the tender stage between April and June with works to commence later this year. item.title: Only 14pc of local primary teachers are men
item.description: There are six times as many women serving as primary school teachers in the Shannonside region as men. New figures have been released by the Education Minister. These new figures, from Minister Hildegarde Naughton, reveal 84 per cent of the country's primary school teachers are female and 16 per cent are male. item.title: Mark Dowd issues squad update following Sligo defeat
item.description: Roscommon senior football manager Mark Dowd says he was pleased with affording as many players game time as he did in this year’s FBD. His Roscommon team lost to Sligo in the FBD shield final in the Connacht Centre of Excellence on Friday night. item.title: Calls Grow for Roscommon County Council to Grit Troublesome Route
item.description: Roscommon County Council are facing calls to add a troublesome route to the local authority's gritting list. The L1612, Ballintobber to Castlerea road, has been described as "lethal." Today's meeting of the Roscommon MD heard that despite adverse weather conditions, the road was not gritted. item.title: Calls for Former South Leitrim Church to Become Tourist Facility
item.description: There are calls for a former church in south Leitrim to be turned into a tourist facility. The building in Drumcong was developed 50 years ago, but is now vacant and in poor condition. It will be auctioned on Thursday, with a guide price of 175,000 euro. item.title: Longford Records Joint Lowest Publicly Funded Athletics Projects Over Five Years
item.description: Longford has had the joint lowest amount of publicly funded athletics projects in the country in the last five years. The Dáil released the numbers last Wednesday. Minister of State at the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport Charlie McConalogue revealed that Longford alongside Laois have had just one athletics project funded by the government since 2020. item.title: Center Parcs seeking to enhance visitor experience in Ballymahon
item.description: Center Parcs have lodged plans to further enhance the visitor experience in Ballymahon. They've applied to Longford County Council for planning to develop a new aerial zipline attraction. The proposed development also included the construction of a single-storey timber canopy for changing facilities. Longford County Planners are due to decide on the application in March.
